name: Energy-Limited Foraging
hypothesis: Previous strategies prioritized cargo volume over energy conservation, forcing agents to deplete their energy reserves to reach maximum capacity (3 units) before depositing. This high-energy cost per trip resulted in premature exhaustion and zero stored food. By switching the mandatory deposit trigger from a cargo-based condition ('carrying') to an energy-based condition ('tired'), agents will stop at the optimal point where they are most fatigued rather than full, balancing movement efficiency with survival. Combined with a fixed rest interval, this ensures agents return home frequently without over-extending their limited energy pool.
